ground_truth.unit: logit coefficient per real dollar of sugar-industry contributions
ground_truth.location: Table 1, District fixed effects, Inflation-adjusted sugar contributions
ground_truth.context: Table 1 ("The Determinants of Voting in Favor of Sugar Reform"), column District fixed effects, row Inflation-adjusted sugar contributions.  Logit; the dependent variable equals 1 for "aye" votes on the two reform amendments to the U.S. sugar program (the 2013 Pitts amendment, H. Amdt. 227 to H.R. 1947, and the 2018 Foxx amendment, H. Amdt. 605 to H.R. 2; aye = a vote against sugar interests) and 0 otherwise.  One observation per House district and vote; the two votes are treated as repeated votes on the same issue. Regressor: inflation-adjusted sugar-industry contributions (all sugar-industry PACs plus individual contributions over $200 from people working in the sugar industry, Center for Responsive Politics) to the incumbent, aggregated from one year before the vote through the end of the calendar year of the vote.  Controls: the American Conservative Union ideology score (ACU, 1-100, higher = more conservative), tenure, the district poverty rate, % with a bachelor's degree, median income, % population over 65, and a dummy for membership on the House agriculture committee.  District fixed effects, so only the districts whose vote outcome changed between the two amendments identify the coefficients.  Probability values from robust standard errors; the table prints coefficient (p), p = 0.001, significant at 1%.

i4r.notes: DP 57 Table 1 col 1 (robust SEs reproduction), -0.0006, p < 0.001.

ground_truth.location: Table 1, Incumbent fixed effects, Inflation-adjusted sugar contributions
ground_truth.context: Table 1, column Incumbent fixed effects, row Inflation-adjusted sugar contributions.  Same logit, outcome, regressor and controls as sugar_contributions_district_fe, with the sample restricted to incumbents who voted on both amendments (the same member in the district for both votes), so the fixed effects are incumbent fixed effects and only the incumbents who changed their vote identify the coefficients.  Robust standard errors; the table prints p = 0.001, significant at 1%.

i4r.notes: DP 57 Table 1 col 2, -0.0004, p < 0.001 (the meta-database row's r_coeff "-.004" is a slip).

ground_truth.context: Table 1, column District fixed effects, row ACU: the American Conservative Union ideology score of the district's representative (1-100, higher = more conservative).  Same district fixed-effects logit as sugar_contributions_district_fe; p = 0.001.

cell.label: claude-code
deviations_manifest: Agriculture-committee coefficient is quasi-separated (R's glm drifts to about -57 rather than Stata's -36.3); not a scored claim.
Contributions variable taken to be totalcont as supplied (assumed already inflation-adjusted by the authors); no further deflation applied.
cell.notes: Two exploratory runs (attempt-1: variable inspection and comparison of the three .dta files, which differ only in totalcont; attempt-2: window totals and switching-sample counts). Final model: logit (glm binomial) of aye (vote == 'Aye', all other responses 0) on totalcont, ACU score (ncu), tenure, poverty, bach, medincome, over65, agcom plus fixed-effect dummies (with a constant), on the units observed for both votes whose vote switched; robust HC0 sandwich SEs scaled by n/(n-1). District FE: district id; 93 switching districts after dropping one with missing tenure, N=186. Incumbent FE: rows with both==1 (same member at both votes), 53 switchers, N=106. Windows: SugarReplicate.dta = baseline (largest totals, 1 year before vote to end of calendar year), SugarReplicate_iter1.dta = calendar-year window, SugarReplicate_iter2.dta = 12 months up to the vote (mapping inferred from file order matching Table 3 row order). Readme .docx read for data provenance only. The first scored run was final; no claim or error iterations. No docker hangs. The paper text was read via the harness copy of paper.txt saved in the session tool-results directory (identical content, output overflow).
